concepts.core_brief: Answer programming questions to leap between safe platforms and cross spike gaps.
Choose valid syntax to charge a ship's blaster and clear asteroids before they hit the convoy.
Arrange flowchart blocks to guide a courier through a maze to the exit.
Use conditional rules to place defenders on lanes where incoming enemies need them.
Use loops to water, tend, and harvest crops in the right order before weather changes.
Solve short code snippets to unlock enchanted doors and reach the dungeon exit.
Sequence commands to route a signal through a firewall grid without triggering alarms.
Use depth variables and sonar readings to navigate safely to a treasure marker.
Match code commands to the beat to clear bugs and keep the music loop intact.
Use flowchart logic to compare clues, rule out suspects, and solve a small case.
Build a recipe loop that prepares orders in the correct sequence before the timer runs out.
Use Boolean rules to choose which windows and doors to barricade as threats approach.
Use flowchart commands to direct archers and protect the castle gate through enemy waves.
Use coordinates to steer a ship around reefs and reach marked island destinations.
Rearrange flowchart-controlled switches to route trains safely to their stations.
Use functions to trigger vine swings and carry the explorer across gaps.
Create sorting rules that send widgets to the correct assembly stations.
Repair timeline logic by placing events in the correct order across two eras.
Declare and assign variables to unlock coffins, gates, and a route out of the castle.
Define simple functions to create and safely classify original test creatures.
Use arithmetic to total groceries, return change, and keep checkout orders moving.
Use decision-tree choices to avoid guards and reach a safe exit.
Assemble syntax-based incantations to cast the correct spell for each obstacle.
Use loops to guide groups of citizens along safe evacuation routes.

concepts.learning_target: API endpoint concepts and data routing
concepts.core_brief: Route encrypted packages to the right API endpoint while avoiding delivery delays.
Use flowchart logic to complete a sequence of harmless exorcism tasks.
Allocate water and supplies across a route so the expedition reaches an oasis.
Set loop boundaries to time flips, catches, and safe landings during a performance.
Use flowcharts to advise a digital ruler through policy choices and consequences.
Use array indexes to place the right training units in matching arena positions.
Use error handling steps to diagnose and patch hull leaks during a deep dive.
Use conditionals to sort sweets by shape and send each batch to the correct bin.
Use flowchart choices to balance habitats and keep wildlife needs in range.
Adjust velocity variables to guide a paddle and return the ball through target zones.
Compare sensor values with thresholds to forecast weather and prepare the station.
Use flowchart paths to cross laser grids and reach a display without triggering alarms.
Use queues and sequencing to guide arrivals to safe runways in order.
Use conditionals to select oven settings and prevent each recipe from over- or under-baking.
Use response vectors to choose the fastest safe route to city emergencies.
Switch flowchart paths to route a friendly ghost train to the correct station.
Apply syntax rules to cross-pollinate plants and grow a set of target flowers.
Use loop iterations to climb a route while respecting safe stopping points.
Use nested coordinate loops to restore missing tiles in a small image.
Use decision blocks to select safe responses to outlaw distractions and protect townsfolk.
Use telescope coordinates to locate stars and identify a target exoplanet pattern.
Use Boolean statements to decide which castle defenses activate against each wave.
Connect flowchart connectors to route water around leaks and restore the neighborhood supply.
Follow dialogue-tree rules to learn clues and complete a small quest chain.

concepts.learning_target: frequency, wave forms, and pattern matching
concepts.core_brief: Adjust frequency and wave settings to compose short patterns that match target sounds.
Arrange quantum-gate flow blocks to transform an input state into a target output.

concepts.learning_target: match flowchart symbols to their roles
concepts.core_brief: Read the shape, know the job: terminals, input/output, processes, and decisions.
Follow one path from start to end, with every step in the right order.

concepts.learning_target: trace and wire a two-way decision
concepts.core_brief: A diamond asks a question; the program follows exactly one branch.

concepts.learning_target: read a loop condition and its back edge
concepts.core_brief: A loop repeats a body while its condition stays true, then exits.
Trace nested decisions and predict which branch a value takes.

concepts.learning_target: identify the properties of an algorithm
concepts.core_brief: An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of unambiguous steps that solves a problem.
Pseudocode uses plain-language keywords to describe an algorithm before coding.
Every useful program takes data in, transforms it, and reports a result.

concepts.learning_target: trace an algorithm with a table of values
concepts.core_brief: Desk checking runs an algorithm by hand, one assignment at a time.

concepts.learning_target: trace linear search and bubble sort
concepts.core_brief: Search looks for one value; sort rearranges all values into order.

concepts.learning_target: identify the parts of a C program
concepts.core_brief: A C program brings in a library, starts at main, runs statements, and returns a status.

concepts.learning_target: follow source code through compilation to an executable
concepts.core_brief: The compiler translates source into an executable and reports syntax errors before the program runs.
Comments explain code to humans; the compiler ignores them completely.

concepts.learning_target: write and trace a first printf program
concepts.core_brief: A first program includes stdio.h, opens main, prints a line, and returns zero.

concepts.learning_target: choose int, float, or char for a value
concepts.core_brief: A data type tells C how much space a value needs and which operations make sense.
A variable can change during a run; a constant is fixed once it is defined.

concepts.learning_target: read input with scanf and print with printf
concepts.core_brief: scanf reads formatted input into a variable address; printf writes formatted output.

concepts.learning_target: predict the result of sequential statements
concepts.core_brief: Sequential statements run top to bottom, and each assignment uses the current value.
An if test chooses one branch; else supplies the path when the test is false.
A for loop initializes a counter, tests it, runs the body, and updates the counter.

concepts.learning_target: read a function definition and call
concepts.core_brief: A function packages a task, takes parameters, returns a result, and is called by name.

concepts.learning_target: choose valid and meaningful variable names
concepts.core_brief: C names start with a letter or underscore, use only letters, digits, and underscores, and cannot be keywords.

concepts.learning_target: declare a variable with a type and name
concepts.core_brief: A declaration gives C a type and a name; the compiler reserves storage for the value.

concepts.learning_target: use = to store a value and == to compare
concepts.core_brief: The single equals sign stores a value; the double equals sign compares two values.
An uninitialized local variable holds an unpredictable value, so initialize it first.

concepts.learning_target: swap two variables with a temporary
concepts.core_brief: Directly copying one variable over another destroys a value; a temporary keeps it safe.

concepts.learning_target: use literals and named constants safely
concepts.core_brief: A literal is written directly in code; a named constant gives that value a readable, protected name.

concepts.learning_target: predict integer division and use an explicit cast
concepts.core_brief: Mixing types converts values; integer division truncates, while a cast can force decimal division.

concepts.learning_target: identify where a local variable can be used
concepts.core_brief: A local variable exists only inside the function or block that declares it.

concepts.learning_target: read and reason about global variables
concepts.core_brief: A global variable is declared outside every function and is visible to the whole file.
Each pair of braces opens a block; a name declared inside is invisible after the block ends.

concepts.learning_target: apply precedence and the modulus operator
concepts.core_brief: Multiplication, division, and modulus bind tighter than addition and subtraction.
score += 5 is shorthand for score = score + 5; the operator updates the same variable.
Comparisons produce 1 for true and 0 for false in C.

concepts.learning_target: combine conditions with and, or, and not
concepts.core_brief: && needs both sides true, || needs one side true, and ! flips a truth value.

concepts.learning_target: control one block with an if test
concepts.core_brief: An if statement runs its body only when the condition is true; braces group the body.

concepts.learning_target: order ranges in an else-if chain
concepts.core_brief: An else-if chain tests conditions in order and runs only the first match.

concepts.learning_target: trace switch cases and break statements
concepts.core_brief: A switch selects one case label; break stops execution from falling into the next case.

concepts.learning_target: trace a while loop and its update
concepts.core_brief: A while loop tests before each pass; the body must move the condition toward false.

concepts.learning_target: read all three parts of a for header
concepts.core_brief: A for header packs initialization, condition, and update into one line.
A do-while loop runs its body once before checking the condition at the bottom.

concepts.learning_target: declare, initialize, and index an array
concepts.core_brief: An array stores a fixed number of same-type values; the first index is 0.

concepts.learning_target: visit every array element with a loop
concepts.core_brief: A traversal uses an index from 0 to size - 1 to visit every element exactly once.

concepts.learning_target: trace a linear search through an array
concepts.core_brief: Linear search checks each element from index 0 until it finds the target or runs out of elements.

concepts.learning_target: read a function return type, name, and body
concepts.core_brief: A function definition states the return type, the name, the parameters, and the body.
Parameters are the names in the definition; arguments are the values supplied by the caller.

concepts.learning_target: trace which value a function returns
concepts.core_brief: return immediately ends the function and sends a value back to the caller.
A syntax error breaks the grammar of C, so the compiler cannot produce an executable.

concepts.learning_target: find code that compiles but computes the wrong result
concepts.core_brief: A logic error is valid C that produces an unintended result; testing reveals it.

concepts.learning_target: guard against division by zero and invalid access
concepts.core_brief: A runtime error happens while the program runs, often from invalid data or an unsafe operation.
